units.translation: Of the genitive and dative forms οὗτινος [of whom], ᾧτινι [to whom], ὧντινων [of whom (pl.)], οἷστισι [to whom (pl.)], the forms ὅτου [of whom], ὅτῳ [to whom] have several examples in Aeschylus, but there are no plural forms ὅτων [of whom (pl.)] and ὅτοισι [to whom (pl.)] for ὧντινων [of whom (pl.)] and οἷστισι [to whom (pl.)]. ὅστις [whoever] and ὅ τι [whatever] coalesce by crasis with καί [and], χὤστις [and whoever] Pers. 502. Ch. 111, χὤτι [and whatever] Sept. 197.
where now ὅπερ [which] has been restored from Etym. M.
And ὅστις ἄν [whoever].
the new plan by whom the scepter and honors are being stripped away

it is easy for one who keeps his foot outside of troubles to give advice

I will tell you clearly everything you wish to learn
grant the favor which we ask
your father bids you to declare the marriages you boast of
one must speak what is fitting, whoever guards the matter
man and woman and whatever is between them

the signal-maker —, who assigned this task

whoever has experience of evils, knows
an ornament that is seemly
there is no torture or device by which Zeus will turn me

and take the opportunity of these things, whoever is swiftest

whoever prays for these things otherwise for this city
lest someone whom we do not see?

who was then in the house
first herself and whoever hates Aegisthus
saying simply, whoever will kill in return
there is no one except one who could shear him
let him know, whoever has learned, not winged by anxieties
where then is the honor, which I received in return?
and she who devised this abomination against her husband —, what do you think?
but whoever has sinned, like this man, and hides murderous hands, we have appeared to him completely
whatever is fated for you, may it happen

whoever betrayed your honor to mortals
